sample_geography_vintage: National NCHS natality files 1987--2023; first births assigned to maternal cohorts 1979--1984; observed maternal ages 12--49; N=10578871
estimator_measurement: First-birth-count-weighted mean after collapsing exact ages to seven four-year model cells and labeling them by midpoints 20 through 44
clustering: none; full national first-birth count target

sample_geography_vintage: National NCHS natality files 1987--2023; first births assigned to maternal cohorts 1979--1984; observed maternal ages 12--49; N=10578871
estimator_measurement: First-birth-count share in model cells beginning at age 30 or later; this classification is identical to exact age at least 30 under the declared operator
clustering: none; full national first-birth count target
uncertainty_type: rounded primary-versus-1975--1980 cohort-window stability scale; not a sampling standard error

sample_geography_vintage: PSID panel; current women ages 18+ who are reference person or spouse; positive IW; valid single-family-unit dwelling; one woman per household-year; 49457 household-years and 4112 women; 2486 treated and 1654 confirmed childless controls
estimator_measurement: Sun--Abraham event-study contrast in occupied rooms from event time -1 to +3 around the first biological child; model analogue branches the same dated risk set into birth and no-birth states and advances both one four-year model period
clustering: person ID; analytic full-covariance clustered standard error for the +3 minus -1 contrast
uncertainty_type: cluster-robust standard error for the four-year contrast
caveat: Earlier leads reject a flat prepath; the contrast can include another birth and remains a provisional rather than causal mapping. In the model, 2019 policies advance both matched branches and 2023 policies govern continuation fertility and housing; the Census age bridge is excluded from the comparison. ACTUALROOMS_ is shifted forward one observed interview before vintage-specific missing codes are applied.
